meta: A breaking-news photo is all over the internet: is it real or made by AI? Watermarks, C2PA, AI labels, their limits, and three steps to check.

muc.title: Real photo or AI photo?
muc.text: Mark sees a breaking-news photo spreading everywhere online, and can't tell whether it's real or made by AI.

muc.title: A hidden mark in the image
muc.text: Bit explains: many AI tools now add a watermark, a hidden mark you can't see with your eyes but a scanner can read.

muc.title: A birth certificate for photos
muc.text: C2PA is a standard that attaches origin information to the file, like a birth certificate for the photo: what made it and when it was edited. On some sites, you can click the Content Credentials icon to see it.

muc.title: Labels on social media
muc.text: Big social networks also label AI-made content, and Europe and many other countries, including Vietnam, are writing rules for marking AI content into law.

muc.title: No label doesn't mean real
muc.text: But the mark can be lost when the image is cropped, screenshotted or reposted. No label doesn't mean the photo is real.

muc.title: Three steps to check
muc.text: For important news, do three things: run a reverse image search, see who posted it first, and compare with mainstream news outlets.

muc.title: Reverse-search a photo
muc.text: Take a strange photo you saw today and use image search to find where it first appeared.
